newsitem.title: USA: Stocks weighed down by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Stocks weighed down by profit-taking.

text.p: Stocks fell Thursday as weakness in retail stocks and renewed profit-taking in technology shares weighed on the market.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 14.35 points at 6,549.49. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 12-9 on active New York Stock Exchange volume of 232 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index was off 12.68 points at 1,236.75.
Investors were reluctant to make major bets ahead of the upcoming wave of corporate profit reports.

"It looks like a bit of profit-taking after the rise we've seen in the last few days," Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney. "You start to get people selling who are worried about interest rates long term."
The Dow fell 45 points Wednesday after a three-session rebound from a sharp sell-off that some on Wall Street described as a needed correction and others as the initial stirrings of a bear market.
The recent gainers came under the gun, with Intel Corp. losing 2-1/8 at 140-1/8.
"The market is tired, players are tired, momentum has slowed," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "The overall feeling is that most players can't wait for the weekend."

Mixed March same-store sales data and news that Sears, Roebuck & Co. may refund payments received from credit card debtors who have filed for bankruptcy hit retailers, traders said. Sears, a Dow component, fell 2-7/8 to 48.
"A lot of the damage is being done by Sears," one trader said. Woolworth Corp. was off 1/2 to 21-7/8 after report its same-store sales fell 3.2 percent.
Kmart Corp. rose 1/8 to 12-5/8 after its March same-store sales, on a consolidated basis, rose 12.7 percent.

Elsewhere, Compaq Computer Corp. said it was buying Microcom Inc., a maker of remote access technologies and modems, for $280 million. Compaq was off 3/4 at 77-3/8, while Microcom jumped 5-3/8 to 15-7/8.
Safeway Inc. fell 3-1/8 to 44-7/8 after the company said a strike by its retail clerks, bakers and meatcutters in Alberta, Canada, will hurt its sales and operating results.
Merck & Co. rose 2-1/8 to 83-5/8 as bargain-hunters moved in following the stock's fall of 3-3/4 points Wednesday on concern over competition for its cholesterol-lowering drugs.
